hints: Focus on finding the longest continuous carbon chain that contains the carbon attached to the OH group, that sets your parent name.
Count that longest chain, it has 5 carbons with the OH on carbon 2, so the parent is pentan-2-ol with two extra methyl groups on the same carbon.
Number to give the OH the lowest possible number, then list the two methyl substituents together to complete the IUPAC name.
walkthrough:
**Draw out the skeleton and find the parent chain**

Think like a teacher with you. Expand the line structure to see every carbon.

$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$$
The longest chain through the C-OH carbon is 5 carbons long, so the parent is pentane.

**Number to give OH the lowest locant**

For alcohols, the OH group always wins for low numbers. Number from the left, close to the OH.

$$\text{C1}-\text{C2}(\text{OH})-\text{C3}-\text{C4}-\text{C5}$$
This gives pentan-2-ol. Numbering from the right would give pentan-4-ol, which is higher, so we reject it.

**Add the side branches**

Look at carbon 3. It has two methyl groups attached to it. That is 3,3-dimethyl.
Put it all together and you get 3,3-dimethylpentan-2-ol.

options.A: Incorrect. This picks butane (4 carbons) as the parent instead of the true longest 5-carbon chain. You should never choose a shorter chain just to make more substituents, always take the longest chain containing the functional group carbon.
options.B: Incorrect. This names a butan-2-ol parent with an ethyl and methyl branch, and puts the OH on a carbon that would have 5 bonds in that naming. The structure has the OH on C2 of a pentane chain, not on a branched quaternary carbon.
options.C: Correct. The longest chain is 5 carbons, numbered to give OH position 2, giving pentan-2-ol, with two methyl groups both on carbon 3. This follows IUPAC rules for longest chain, lowest locant for the principal functional group, and alphabetical substituents.
options.D: Incorrect. The chain and numbers are right, but the functional group naming is wrong. When OH is the principal functional group, the suffix must be -ol (pentan-2-ol), not hydroxy. The prefix hydroxy- is only used when another higher priority group like a carboxylic acid is present.
